name: Car Dealerships
h1: AI Phone Agent for Car Dealerships: Sales and Service Calls
metaDescription: Calldesk answers dealership calls for sales, service and parts: vehicle availability inquiries, test-drive booking and service scheduling by department.
intro: A dealership's phone is really three phones: sales, service and parts, and they behave differently. Sales calls are driven by online listings and ad campaigns. Someone sees a used truck at a good price and calls to ask if it is still on the lot. Service calls come from owners who need an oil change or hear a noise, and they peak on Monday mornings and before holidays. Parts calls from body shops and do-it-yourselfers want a part number checked. Switchboards often route everyone to whoever picks up, and a lead that sits on hold or gets bounced to voicemail while salespeople are with customers will often try the next dealer. A Calldesk agent can answer as the dealership's AI assistant, ask which department is needed, give inventory answers from information you load, such as the units in a current knowledge base, and offer a test-drive slot on a connected calendar. Service callers get drop-off times and common answers. Trade-in value, financing terms and out-the-door prices are never settled by the agent; those go to a salesperson. Outbound batch calls can invite owners to service specials, with the vehicle and name as variables.
callTypes: Used-car shoppers asking if a listed vehicle is still available
New-car buyers asking about stock, color and delivery timing
Trade-in and financing questions that must reach a salesperson
Service customers booking maintenance or recall work
Parts counter inquiries from body shops and owners
Outbound invitations to owners whose lease or service interval is coming up

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks for calling the dealership. I'm the dealership's AI assistant. Are you calling for sales, service or parts?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Sales. I saw a used pickup online, the gray one with 40,000 miles.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: My information shows a gray pickup with about 40,000 miles listed as available as of this morning. Would you like to come see it?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: Yes. Can you tell me the lowest price?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I can share the listed price. Negotiating is something our sales team does in person or by phone. May I get your name?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thanks, Alicia. Are you planning to trade in a vehicle, or paying with financing?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: I have a trade, and I'd like financing.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I'll note both for the salesperson. A test drive is open Saturday at 11 or 2. Which works?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Booked, and I'll tell your salesperson about the trade-in and financing interest.

setupSteps: Create an agent from the receptionist template that asks sales, service or parts first, and set up separate transfer targets for each department.
Load the current inventory summary or a link-based knowledge entry for in-stock vehicles and refresh it on a schedule you can keep.
Add extraction fields for name, phone, vehicle of interest, trade-in, financing interest and desired timeframe.
Connect a calendar for test drives and service drop-offs, and keep a transfer to a live salesperson during selling hours.
Test with vehicle-specific scenarios, publish, and send leads to your CRM through completed-call webhooks.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Routes the call to sales, service or parts based on what the caller needs, and hands hot leads to a salesperson.
Holds hours, department details and a current vehicle list so callers hear accurate availability.
Schedules test drives and service drop-offs without tying up a salesperson.
Captures the vehicle of interest, trade-in and financing interest for the CRM.
Pushes completed-call data to your CRM so leads are logged at once.

considerations: Advertising, pricing and financing statements are regulated, including truth-in-lending and unfair practices rules. The agent should state the prices and terms you have approved, and never discuss financing terms or credit decisions.
Keep the agent from confirming availability if your inventory feed is not current; a stale answer is a risk. Assign someone to maintain the knowledge base.
Outbound calls to leads or past customers are subject to consent and Do Not Call rules, including TCPA in the United States. Check with counsel before running batches.
Credit applications involve sensitive data; do not collect it through the agent unless you have reviewed the legal and security requirements.

faq.q: Can it tell a shopper whether a specific car is on the lot?
faq.a: Yes, based on the inventory information you give it. Accuracy depends on keeping that information updated; the agent has no built-in link to inventory systems.
No. It repeats listed prices and passes negotiation to a salesperson. Configure it to say so plainly if a caller asks for the lowest price.

faq.q: Can service and sales use different numbers?
faq.a: Yes. Use separate numbers and agents, or one number with a department question at the start, whichever suits your phone system.

faq.q: How does it work with my existing phone system?
faq.a: Calldesk is bring-your-own-carrier on every plan, or you can add numbers from Calldesk. Forwarding your main line to a Calldesk number is a common way to try it.

faq.q: Can it call people who inquired online?
faq.a: It can place outbound calls to a list, but to people who have agreed to be contacted that way. Consult counsel on what your web forms actually permit.
